body:
Why industries develop in particular places

Industrial location depends on access to raw materials, energy, labour, capital, transport, water and markets. In Gujarat, coastal access, agricultural production, petroleum resources and established commercial centres have contributed to the development of specialised industrial clusters.

An industrial cluster is a geographical concentration of enterprises engaged in related economic activities. Firms within a cluster often benefit from shared labour skills, suppliers, infrastructure and markets.

The mainland industrial belt

A major concentration of industries extends through mainland Gujarat from Ahmedabad towards Vadodara, Bharuch, Surat and Vapi. This belt benefits from relatively developed transport networks, urban markets and access to coastal ports.

CentreImportant industrial association
AhmedabadCotton textiles, pharmaceuticals
Sanand, Ahmedabad districtAutomobiles and engineering
VadodaraPetrochemicals, engineering and pharmaceuticals
Ankleshwar, Bharuch districtChemicals and pharmaceuticals
Dahej, Bharuch districtPetrochemicals and port-based industries
SuratDiamond cutting and polishing, textiles
Hazira, Surat districtSteel, engineering and port-based industries
Vapi, Valsad districtChemicals, dyes and other manufacturing

Ahmedabad and Surat

Ahmedabad developed historically as a major cotton textile centre. Its industrial growth was supported by access to cotton-producing regions, labour, capital and transport.

Surat developed a specialised diamond-cutting and polishing industry together with a substantial textile industry, particularly synthetic and man-made fabrics.

The diamond industry illustrates the importance of skilled labour, specialised production networks and international trade. Surat is a diamond-processing centre; its importance does not depend on local diamond mining.

Bharuch, Vadodara and Vapi

The Vadodara–Bharuch industrial region is especially associated with chemical and petrochemical industries. Ankleshwar is a major chemical manufacturing centre, while Dahej combines industrial activity with coastal port access.

Vapi, in southern Gujarat near the Maharashtra boundary, is another established industrial centre associated with chemicals and dyes.

Industrial centres of Saurashtra

CentrePrincipal association
JamnagarPetroleum refining and brass components
RajkotEngineering, foundries and machine tools
MorbiCeramic products and clocks
AlangShip recycling
VeravalFishing and seafood processing
PorbandarCement and coastal economic activities

Jamnagar's petroleum-refining industry benefits from maritime access, enabling the movement of crude oil and refined products. The city is also historically associated with brass-component manufacturing.

Morbi's ceramic cluster produces tiles, sanitaryware and related products. Rajkot's engineering cluster has developed around machine tools, foundries and manufacturing enterprises.

Resource and agricultural industries

Region or centreEconomic association
Kachchh and Little RannSalt production
KachchhCement and port-linked industries
AnandDairy processing and cooperative dairying
Unjha, Mehsana districtSpice and isabgol trade
Coastal SaurashtraFishing and seafood processing

Salt production in the Rann and coastal lowlands benefits from saline water, extensive flat land and strong evaporation. Water is concentrated through evaporation until salt crystallises.

Cement industries require limestone and other mineral inputs. Their location in parts of Saurashtra and Kachchh reflects the availability of mineral resources and transport facilities.

Anand's dairy industry is associated with cooperative milk collection, processing and marketing. Its industrial development is therefore closely connected to agricultural and livestock-based activities.

Industrial locations and their geographical advantages

Industries may depend on different location factors even within the same state. For example, salt production is closely related to climate and saline environments, petroleum refining benefits from access to bulk maritime transport, and diamond processing depends heavily on labour skills and established trade networks.

Prelims focus

  • Surat–diamond processing and textiles; Ahmedabad–cotton textiles.
  • Jamnagar–petroleum refining and brass components.
  • Morbi–ceramics; Rajkot–engineering and machine tools.
  • Ankleshwar and Vapi–chemical industries.
  • Anand–cooperative dairy industry; Alang–ship recycling.
  • Trap: A processing centre is not necessarily a raw-material-producing centre.

[Sources: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, State Profile of Gujarat, industrial cluster listings; Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation, Industrial Estates and Clusters information; NITI Aayog, Export Preparedness Index 2024, Gujarat state profile; National Dairy Development Board, information on dairying in Gujarat; Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Vapi Chemicals and Dyes Cluster information; Survey of India, Gujarat State Map, 2026; online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]

body:
Protected areas and geographical habitats

A protected area is a geographically defined area managed for the conservation of biodiversity and natural habitats. National parks and wildlife sanctuaries are important categories of protected areas under Indian wildlife law.

A national park generally has stricter restrictions on the exercise of resource-use rights than a wildlife sanctuary. Wildlife sanctuaries also protect animals and habitats, but certain regulated activities or recognised rights may be permitted under applicable law.

Gujarat's protected areas represent several contrasting habitats, including dry deciduous forests, saline deserts, grasslands, wetlands, coastal marine ecosystems and moist forested hills.

The four national parks

Gujarat has 4 national parks in the Wildlife Institute of India's Gujarat protected-area inventory consulted on 26 November 2026.

National parkLocationPrincipal habitat or wildlife
GirJunagadh region, southern SaurashtraDry forest and Asiatic lion
Blackbuck, VelavadarBhavnagar districtGrasslands and blackbuck
VansdaNavsari districtForested hills of South Gujarat
Marine, Gulf of KachchhJamnagar coastal regionCoral reefs, mangroves and marine life

Gir National Park

Gir is associated with the conservation of the Asiatic lion. Its dry deciduous forest, scrub vegetation and water sources form an important habitat for lions and their prey.

The Gir National Park and the surrounding Gir Wildlife Sanctuary are distinct protected-area designations. The larger lion landscape extends beyond their boundaries into other parts of Saurashtra, including areas of Amreli and Gir Somnath.

Blackbuck National Park, Velavadar

Velavadar lies in Bhavnagar district near the Gulf of Khambhat. Unlike Gir's predominantly forested landscape, Velavadar is especially associated with open grasslands. The blackbuck is its characteristic mammal, and the park also provides habitat for grassland birds.

Vansda National Park

Vansda, also written as Bansda, lies in present-day Navsari district. It protects forest vegetation in the relatively high-rainfall southern Gujarat region. Its habitat differs considerably from the dry grasslands and saline landscapes of western Gujarat.

Marine National Park

The Marine National Park lies along the southern side of the Gulf of Kachchh, particularly in the Jamnagar coastal region. Its protected habitats include coral reefs, mangroves, islands and intertidal areas. Pirotan and Narara are well-known locations associated with the gulf's marine biodiversity.

It was established in 1982 and is recognised as India's first marine national park.

Important wildlife sanctuaries

SanctuaryLocationAssociation
Indian Wild AssLittle Rann of KachchhIndian wild ass
Kachchh DesertGreat Rann of KachchhSaline desert and wetland birds
Narayan SarovarWestern KachchhArid habitat and chinkara
Kachchh Bustard, LalaAbdasa region, KachchhGreat Indian bustard habitat
BardaPorbandar–Devbhumi Dwarka regionDry forest and hill habitat
JessoreBanaskanthaSloth bear and Aravalli Hills
Balaram-AmbajiBanaskanthaAravalli forest habitat
JambughodaPanchmahal–Chhota Udepur regionEastern Gujarat forests
RatanmahalDahod regionSloth bear
ShoolpaneshwarNarmada districtForested hills of the Narmada basin
PurnaDang districtSouthern hill forests
KhijadiyaJamnagar districtFreshwater and coastal wetland habitats

Great Rann and Little Rann wildlife distinctions

The Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary is principally associated with the Little Rann of Kachchh. The Indian wild ass is adapted to open, dry and saline environments.

The Kachchh Desert Wildlife Sanctuary is associated with the Great Rann. Parts of this region become seasonally inundated and provide important habitat for waterbirds, including flamingos.

These sanctuaries should not be confused merely because both lie within the wider Rann landscape.

Prelims focus

  • Gir National Park–Asiatic lion.
  • Velavadar National Park–blackbuck and grassland.
  • Vansda National Park–Navsari district and southern forests.
  • Marine National Park–Gulf of Kachchh, established in 1982.
  • Jessore and Ratanmahal are associated with sloth bears.
  • Trap: The Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary is associated with the Little Rann, not the Great Rann.

[Sources: Wildlife Institute of India, Wildlife Database, Gujarat national park and wildlife sanctuary inventory; Wildlife Institute of India, Gujarat protected-area directory; Gujarat Forest Department, protected-area information; Gujarat Tourism, Vansda National Park and Marine National Park information; Survey of India, Gujarat State Map, 2026; online sources consulted 26 November 2026. Present-day district names are used in place of older parent-district names where boundaries have changed.]

body:
Wetlands and the Ramsar Convention

Wetlands are areas where water covers the land or remains near its surface permanently or seasonally. They include lakes, marshes, reservoirs, coastal lagoons and intertidal habitats.

The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran, for the conservation and wise use of wetlands. A wetland designated under the Convention is recognised as a wetland of international importance.

Ramsar designation is distinct from declaration as a national park or wildlife sanctuary under Indian law. A wetland may possess both Ramsar status and a domestic protected-area designation.

Ramsar sites of Gujarat

The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change's national inventory dated 5 June 2026 records 5 Ramsar sites in Gujarat. The following table uses that dated official inventory.

WetlandLocationDesignation year
NalsarovarAhmedabad–Surendranagar region2012
Thol LakeMehsana district2021
Wadhvana WetlandVadodara district2021
Khijadia Wildlife SanctuaryJamnagar district2021
Chhari DhandKachchh district2025

Nalsarovar

Nalsarovar, also written as Nal Sarovar, is a shallow inland wetland located between mainland Gujarat and Saurashtra. It is an important habitat for resident and migratory waterbirds.

It became Gujarat's first Ramsar site in 2012. The surrounding lowland region is known as Nalkantha.

Thol Lake

Thol Lake lies in Mehsana district, north-west of Ahmedabad. It is a shallow artificial freshwater wetland associated with irrigation storage and bird conservation.

Wadhvana Wetland

Wadhvana is located in Vadodara district near Dabhoi. The reservoir supports waterbirds and provides an example of a human-created water body that has acquired international ecological importance.

Khijadia Wildlife Sanctuary

Khijadia, also written as Khijadiya, lies near Jamnagar on the southern side of the Gulf of Kachchh. Its ecological importance arises partly from the close occurrence of freshwater and saline coastal wetland habitats.

Chhari Dhand

Chhari Dhand is a seasonal wetland in Kachchh, associated with the Banni grassland region and the surrounding saline landscape. Monsoon rainfall and runoff create an extensive seasonal water body, which provides feeding and resting habitat for waterbirds.

Its Ramsar designation date is 16 June 2025, while its addition was publicly announced on 30 January 2026. The designation date and announcement date must therefore be distinguished.

Comparison of wetland environments

Wetland typeExamples
Shallow inland wetlandNalsarovar
Artificial freshwater storageThol, Wadhvana
Coastal freshwater and saline habitatsKhijadia
Seasonal wetland in an arid saline regionChhari Dhand

Wetlands support biodiversity by providing feeding grounds, breeding habitats and resting areas for birds. Depending on their geographical setting, they may also store floodwater, recharge groundwater and sustain local livelihoods.

Not every important wetland is automatically a Ramsar site. International designation requires recognition under the Convention.

Prelims focus

  • Nalsarovar was Gujarat's first Ramsar site, designated in 2012.
  • Thol is in Mehsana; Wadhvana is in Vadodara.
  • Khijadia is in Jamnagar and contains contrasting freshwater and saline habitats.
  • Chhari Dhand is a seasonal wetland of Kachchh.
  • Chhari Dhand was designated on 16 June 2025 and announced on 30 January 2026.
  • Trap: Ramsar designation does not automatically make a wetland a national park.

[Sources: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Ramsar Sites of India as on 05.06.2026, Gujarat entries; Ramsar Sites Information Service, site records for Nalsarovar, Thol Lake Wildlife Sanctuary, Wadhvana Wetland, Khijadia Wildlife Sanctuary and Chhari Dhand; Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, January 2026 announcement of new Ramsar sites; online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]
